 Order
This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.PC. praying to enlarge the petitioner/accused No.1 on bail in Cr.No.193/2022 of Yeshwanthapura Police Station.
2. Charge sheet is filed for offences punishable under Sections 304B, 302, 498A, 201 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent- State and perused the material on record.
4.
Deceased Lakshmidevi is the wife of the petitioner.
First informant is the brother of the deceased.
The marriage of Lakshmidevi was performed with the NC: 2023:KHC:19447 petitioner about five years prior to the date of the incident.
At the time of marriage certain gold ornaments were given and the marriage expenses were met by the complainant's side.
For about one year, the deceased was looked after properly.
Thereafter, she was subjected to physical and mental cruelty by the accused.
It is alleged that the petitioner was demanding her to get Rs.2 lakhs from her parental home and also to get a bracelet for him.
He was telling her that he will marry some other girl so that he will get more dowry and thus torturing the deceased.
He was also having illicit relationship with another woman and he used to tell the deceased that if she dies he can live with another woman happily.
5. The deceased Lakshmidevi was found dead in a suspicious circumstance in the early hours of 04.06.2022.

As per the complaint averments a person by name Gangadhar informed the Narasimhayya @ Narashimha vs State Of Karnataka By on 6 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188758709/
2 complainant about the death of his sister.

sentences.text: It is alleged by the prosecution that at the instigation of accused Nos.2 to 5, petitioner/accused No.1 NC: 2023:KHC:19447 strangulated the deceased with a veil and committed her murder.
6. As per post mortem report, cause of death is due to asphyxia secondary to strangulation.
A veil has been recovered at the instance of the accused petitioner.
It is opined by the doctor that strangulation can be done with the said material.
7. There are prima facie materials collected against the petitioner.
There are specific allegations that the petitioner was subjecting the deceased to physical and mental torture.
The submission of the learned counsel for petitioner that the petitioner is innocent and he has not committed any offence cannot be accepted in view of the prima facie material collected against him.
The offence allegedly committed by the petitioner is heinous in nature.
Grant of bail to other accused persons is also not a ground to enlarge the petitioner on bail since specific allegations are against him.
Considering the nature and gravity of NC: 2023:KHC:19447 the offence, this is not a fit case to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Petition is dismissed.
8. Observations made in this order is confined to the disposal of the petition only.
